In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the development of the English word-final voicelessness stops (codas), BP speakers go through a developmental stage characterized by the phenomenon known as Onset-Nuclei Sharing (ONS).
ONS is an emergent property of the developing grammars of BP speakers, which arises as a result of the interaction between the phonetic input and the phonological grammar of English.
, in the acquisition of codas, BP speakers are not simply acquiring the English phonological system, but rather, they are also acquiring a new way to syllabify the input.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the acquisition of English coda consonants by BP speakers is not simply a matter of the acquisition of the feature [+voice] in word-final position, as is usually assumed in the literature, but rather it is a process of syllable structure reorganization, which involves the reorganization of both onset and nucleus features, as well as the reorganization of the syllable template itself.
the phenomenon of ONS is a developmental stage of the acquisition of English by BP speakers, and that it is not an idiosyncratic phenomenon of the Brazilian Portuguese speakers.

the phenomenon of ONS, which has been documented in a number of studies (e.g., Goad 2002; Goad & Brasher 2007; Brasher & Goad 2010) is a natural consequence of the acquisition of the English phonology and that, in the case of BP speakers, it is an intermediate developmental stage of the acquisition of codas by BP learners.
The main takeaway from our work is that

ONS provides a useful tool for the analysis of variable phonological development, as well as for the study of language change in progress, in particular, in cases where the acquisition of a new language involves the restructuring of a phonological system.
the phenomenon of ONS is not only an epiphenomenon, but also a crucial part of the acquisition of English by BP speakers.
the phenomenon of Ons-Nuc sharing provides a principled account for why some BP speakers produce codas that are not found in BP.
